subject: Request: Multi-year rate covenant & renewal protection for BlueStone Health
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Deal Desk <dealdesk@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Request: Multi-year rate covenant & renewal protection for BlueStone Health

Folks,

BlueStone (large public health system in SG) signed up for a pilot last quarter and wants a 3-year committed term. Commercial asks: a 36-month price covenant (no increases on unit pricing for 36 months), an annual uplift cap of 8% (they've suggested index-based increases but want a ceiling), and a renewal protection clause that guarantees renewal pricing will not exceed the greater of our then-list price or their prior-year effective rate plus the uplift cap.

Why escalated: this deviates from our standard 24-month price-lock and we usually cap uplifts at 5-6% for multi-year contracts. Customer is strategic for APAC expansion and has a procurement deadline next week.

Attachments: BlueStone_RFP-pricing-model.xlsx (pricing workbook), BlueStone_Redlines.pdf (their legal edits), SOW-draft.docx (work scope).

Ask: executive approval for exception to policy to grant a 36-month price covenant with an 8% uplift cap and renewal protection as described. If full approval isn't possible, need recommended counter-proposal we can present today.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0123
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Deal Desk <dealdesk@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 11:08:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: Multi-year rate covenant & renewal protection for BlueStone Health

Marcus —

I reviewed the redlines. Key legal concerns: the renewal protection language is open-ended and could lock us into sub-market pricing if our cost structure improves. Also need explicit language for force majeure and capacity-based price adjustments (GPU cost pass-through). We can accept a fixed covenant window, but need a clear mechanism for extraordinary events.

If you want to proceed with a 36-month covenant, Legal recommends: (1) include a carve-out for materially increased cloud/GPU costs linked to published indices; (2) define renewal protection as a one-time right limited to the first renewal only; (3) require a 90-day notice on price changes post-covenant.

I can produce proposed language by EOD.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 13:41:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: Multi-year rate covenant & renewal protection for BlueStone Health

Quick finance take —

We ran the attached workbook. Granting a 36-month lock at the requested Tiers increases our expected unit cost exposure under several scenarios. With an 8% uplift cap, worst-case (high inflation + GPU price increases) the NPV of margin erosion across 36 months is material. Finance comfortable with: 30-month lock + 6% uplift cap or 36-month lock with a 7% cap paired with the legal carve-outs Laura suggested.

If this is strategic (APAC beachhead), we could approve higher flexibility if we structure a performance step (growth-based repricing) after year 2 — e.g., if ARR grows >20% year-on-year, uplift reverts to market index.

Ben Carter
Director, Finance — Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 07:43:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Request: Multi-year rate covenant & renewal protection for BlueStone Health

Adding GTM/leadership perspective. BlueStone is flagged as a top-10 strategic target for APAC. We need demonstrable pricing stability to close enterprise procurement cycles with their network hospitals. If we push too hard on uplift or shorten the covenant we'll likely lose momentum.

Proposed compromise for approval:
- 36-month price covenant on unit rates, subject to carve-outs for extraordinary increases in cloud/GPU costs (as Laura outlines).
- Uplift cap: 7% annual (midpoint between finance and sales).
- Renewal protection: limited to the first renewal only; customer can exercise within 60 days prior to renewal; after that standard renewal negotiation applies.
- Include a growth-trigger clause: if customer ARR increases >25% in a 12-month period, pricing can be rebalanced to list + 3% (protects Redwood economics).

If leadership signs off on that language, I'll take it to customer today.

Marissa Cole
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 18:05:00 +0000
Subject: Approval: 36-month covenant with 7% uplift cap (conditional) — BlueStone Health

Marissa / team —

After reviewing the business case and risk mitigations, I approve the exception on the following conditions:

1) 36-month price covenant is approved subject to legal carve-outs for material GPU/cloud cost increases and force majeure.
2) Uplift cap set at 7% annually.
3) Renewal protection limited to first renewal only and must be exercised by customer within a 60-day window prior to renewal.
4) Include the growth-trigger clause Marissa suggested: if ARR growth >25% in any 12-month rolling period, Redwood reserves the right to rebalance pricing to list + 3% for the next period.
4) Deal must include a non-refundable 90-day implementation deposit and a signed SOW within 30 days.

Marissa, please send the redlined contract with these points to BlueStone legal and get confirmation by the procurement deadline. Marcus — update the HubSpot deal with the approved terms and inform customer that final SOW/signatures needed to lock.

Thanks —
Stephanie Nguyen
VP, Commercial Operations — Redwood Inference
